{{Short description|Topology on the space of semimartingales}}
In [[Martingale (probability theory)|martingale theory]], '''Émery topology''' is a [[topology]] on the space of [[semimartingale]]s. The topology is used in [[financial mathematics]]. The class of [[stochastic integral]]s with general [[predictable process|predictable]] integrands coincides with the [[Closure (topology)|closure]] of the set of all simple integrals.<ref name="Kardaras">{{cite journal|first1=Constantinos|last1=Kardaras|title=On the closure in the Emery topology of semimartingale wealth-process sets|journal=Annals of Applied Probability|volume=23|number=4|pages=1355 - 1376|date=2013|doi=10.1214/12-AAP872|doi-access=free|arxiv=1108.0945}}</ref>

The topology was introduced in 1979 by the French mathematician [[Michel Émery]].<ref>{{cite journal|first1=Michel|last1=Émery|title=Une topologie sur l'espace des semimartingales|journal=Séminaire de probabilités de Strasbourg|volume=13|date=1979|pages=260-280|url=http://www.numdam.org/item/SPS_1979__13__260_0/}}</ref>

== Definition ==
Let <math>(\Omega,\mathcal{A},\{\mathcal{F_t}\},P)</math> be a [[Filtration (probability theory)|filtered]] probability space, where the filtration satisfies the [[usual conditions]] and <math>T\in (0,\infty)</math>. Let <math>\mathcal{S}(P)</math> be the space of real semimartingales and <math>\mathcal{E}(1)</math> the space of simple [[Predictable process|predictable]] processes <math>H</math> with <math>|H|=1</math>. 

We define
:<math>\|X\|_{\mathcal{S}(P)}:=\sup\limits_{H\in \mathcal{E}(1)}\mathbb{E}\left[1\wedge \left(\sup\limits_{t\in[0,T]}|(H\cdot X)_t|\right)\right].</math>

Then <math>(\mathcal{S}(P),d)</math> with the metric <math>d(X,Y):=\|X-Y\|_{\mathcal{S}(P)}</math> is a [[complete metric space]] and the induced topology is called '''Émery topology'''.<ref>{{cite journal|first1=M. |last1=De Donno|first2=M.|last2=Pratelli|title=A theory of stochastic integration for bond markets|journal=Annals of Applied Probability|volume=15|number=4|pages=2773 - 2791|date=2005|doi=10.1214/105051605000000548|arxiv=math/0602532}}</ref><ref name="Kardaras" />
